newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell's profits slip as it completes transition.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell's profits slip as it completes transition.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp. said Tuesday that its profits declined by 12 percent in its second quarter as it exited the auto components business and completed its transformation into an electronics company.

Rockwell, which manufactures industrial automation systems, semiconductors and avionics and communications equipment, said its net income for the three months ended March 31 fell to $189 million, or 87 cents a share, from $214 million, or 98 cents a share, a year earlier.
The company said, however, that net income from continuing operations climbed by 28 percent to $155 million, or 72 cents a share, from $121 million, or 55 cents a share.
It added that sales expanded by 6 percent to $1.9 billion from $1.8 billion, led by double-digit growth in its automation and avionics and communications businesses.
Rockwell's stock jumped by $2.375 to $64.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said its latest quarterly earnings excluded the automotive components business, which was being reported as "discontinued operations."
The prior year's quarter included the earnings of the discontinued automotive business as well as those of its aerospace and defence and graphic systems businesses, which have also been divested.
Rockwell, which is based in Seal Beach, Calif., said its revenue growth was paced by its industrial automation unit, which grew sales by 10 percent to $1.1 billion from $1.0 billion.
Semiconductor sales, however, fell by 15 percent -- from a record quarter last year -- as it switched over to producing new, higher-speed modem chipsets.
